summary:
Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive educational website that brings the stories of NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars to life. Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and some use of ChatGPT it combines cinematic scrolling, NASA photographs, interactive mission stories, and a quiz to make space science engaging and accessible.

The website features Apollo’s Lunar Roving Vehicles, the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), and much more. Visitors discover what each piece of equipment did, how it supported exploration, and what happened after its mission ended. The project also explores the challenges of recovering equipment and presents ideas for documentation, preservation, and future reuse.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming technical mission information into visual storytelling that young learners can explore at their own pace. It encourages visitors to distinguish potentially harmful debris from valuable scientific and historical artifacts. These machines are more than objects left behind, they represent human ingenuity, scientific discovery, and lessons for more responsible exploration of other worlds.
details:
Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive educational website developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project explores the stories of equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars, highlighting their contributions to space exploration and the importance of responsible space exploration.

Our website takes visitors on a cinematic journey using scrolling animations, interactive mission stories, NASA photographs, and an educational quiz. It features three examples: the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles, the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), and Perseverance’s parachute and backshell. Visitors learn how these machines worked, what they achieved, and why they were left behind.

We developed the website using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, GSAP, and ScrollTrigger, with Visual Studio Code for development and GitHub Pages for publishing. NASA research materials and photographs support our educational content.

What makes our project creative is its storytelling approach. Instead of displaying scientific information through traditional articles, we transform it into an immersive visual experience that makes learning engaging, especially for younger audiences.

Our team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, environmental concerns, and the challenges of recovering equipment from extreme environments. We also explored future possibilities for preserving, reusing, and recycling space materials.

Ultimately, our project aims to inspire curiosity, promote sustainable space exploration, and remind people that abandoned equipment is more than space junk—it represents humanity’s achievements and discoveries.
